blocks.text: Frazali fe'llar: go in, get up, come back

**Frazali fe'l** (phrasal verb) — fe'l + kichik so'z: **in**, **out**, **on**, **off**, **up**, **down**, **away**, **back**, **over**, **round**. Bu kichik so'z fe'lga yo'nalish yoki yangi ma'no qo'shadi: go — bormoq, go **in** — kirmoq, go **out** — chiqmoq, go **back** — qaytib bormoq. O'zbek tilida xuddi shu vazifani ko'makchi fe'l bajaradi: «chiqib **ketmoq**», «qaytib **kelmoq**», «yiqilib **tushmoq**». Ya'ni o'zbekcha `-ib` + ko'makchi fe'l ko'pincha inglizcha fe'l + kichik so'zga to'g'ri keladi.

Ko'p frazali fe'llarning ma'nosi oson: fe'l + yo'nalish. Ularni juftlikda, qarama-qarshi ma'no bilan o'rganish qulay: come **in** ↔ go **out**, sit **down** ↔ stand **up**, get **on** ↔ get **off**, go **away** ↔ come **back**. Bu darsdagi fe'llar **to'ldiruvchisiz** ishlatiladi: The door was open, so I went **in**. — kichik so'zdan keyin hech narsa shart emas.

items.text: Please **sit down** and make yourself comfortable.
The children **ran out** into the garden.
I'm **going out** now, but I'll **be back** at six.

blocks.text: Ko'chma ma'no: so'zma-so'z tarjima qilib bo'lmaydi

Ba'zi frazali fe'llarning ma'nosini qismlaridan topib bo'lmaydi — ularni yangi so'z sifatida yodlash kerak: **break down** («buzilib qolmoq»), **look out** («ehtiyot bo'l!»), **take off** (samolyot — «havoga ko'tarilmoq»), **give up** («taslim bo'lmoq, voz kechmoq»), **get up** («o'rnidan turmoq», uyqudan keyin), **grow up** («katta bo'lmoq»).

items.text: My old laptop **broke down** in the middle of the exam.
**Watch out** — there's a hole in the road!

blocks.text: Frazali fe'lda zamon, inkor va savol faqat **fe'l** qismida bildiriladi, kichik so'z o'zgarmaydi: get up → **got** up → have **got** up → is **getting** up. Inkor va savol oddiy fe'ldagidek: I **didn't** get up early. What time **do** you get up? Kichik so'z fe'ldan keyin, o'z o'rnida qoladi.

items.text: What time **did** you **get up** this morning?
We **aren't going out** tonight — we're too tired.
items.translation: Bugun kechqurun **hech qayerga chiqmaymiz** — juda charchadik.

blocks.text: Frazali fe'ldan keyin predlog ham kelishi mumkin — u qayerdan yoki qayerga ekanini aytadi: come back **from** London, run away **from** the dog, get out **of** the car, look out **of** the window, look up **at** the sky. Ba'zi birikmalar yaxlit ma'noga ega: get on **with** (chiqishmoq), look forward **to** (intiqlik bilan kutmoq), run out **of** (tugab qolmoq).

items.text: Aziz **came back from** London with presents for everyone.
items.translation: Aziz Londondan hammaga sovg'a bilan **qaytib keldi**.

items.text: Don't **look out of** the window during the test.

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «return back» → **come back** yoki **return** (bu «qaytib kelmoq» dan so'zma-so'z tarjima; return ning o'zida «back» ma'nosi bor); «I stood up at seven» (uyqudan) → I **got up** at seven; **wake up** — uyg'onmoq, **get up** — o'rnidan turmoq: I woke up at six but got up at seven; «go out from the room» → go **out of** the room; «enter in the room» → **go into** the room yoki **enter** the room.
Frazali fe'llarni juftlikda yodlang: come in ↔ go out, sit down ↔ stand up, get on ↔ get off, go away ↔ come back. Har biriga o'zingiz haqingizda bitta gap tuzing: I usually **get up** at 7.

Bog'lanish: to'ldiruvchili frazali fe'llar (put on your coat / put it on) → 115-dars; frazali fe'llar ro'yxati → 121–122-darslar (ilovalar); fe'l + predlog (listen to, wait for) → 113-dars; harakat predloglari (into, out of, through) → 110-dars.

examples.title: **in** and **out**: come in, go out, get in
examples.description: **in** — ichkariga, **out** — tashqariga: «kirmoq», «chiqmoq», «chiqib ketmoq». **go out** ning yana bir ma'nosi — «biror joyga (dam olgani) chiqmoq».

sentences.text: Please **come in** and sit down.
It started to rain, so we **went in**.
Madina **went out** an hour ago, but she'll be back soon.
sentences.translation: Madina bir soat oldin **chiqib ketdi**, lekin tez orada qaytadi.

sentences.text: Don't **go out** without your coat — it's freezing.
The door was open, so the cat **got out**.
sentences.translation: Eshik ochiq qolgan ekan, mushuk **chiqib ketibdi**.

sentences.text: Are you **going out** tonight, or are you staying at home?
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun **biror joyga chiqasanmi** yoki uyda qolasanmi?

sentences.text: The museum was full, so we couldn't **get in**.
sentences.translation: Muzey odamga to'la edi, shuning uchun **kira olmadik**.

sentences.text: Bekzod **came in**, said hello and went straight to his room.
sentences.translation: Bekzod **kirib keldi**, salom berdi-yu, to'g'ri xonasiga o'tdi.

sentences.text: Let's **eat out** tonight — I'm too tired to cook.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun **tashqarida ovqatlanaylik** — ovqat qilishga holim yo'q.

sentences.text: **Breathe in** slowly, then **breathe out**.

examples.title: **up** and **down**: get up, sit down, fall down
examples.description: **up** — yuqoriga, **down** — pastga: o'rnidan turmoq, o'tirmoq, yiqilmoq, yotmoq. Narx va quyosh haqida ham: **go up** / **go down**.

sentences.text: **Sit down**, please — the film is starting.
Everybody **stood up** when the teacher came in.
I usually **get up** at seven, but today I **got up** at nine.
sentences.translation: Odatda soat yettida **turaman**, bugun esa to'qqizda **turdim**.

sentences.text: Grandpa **fell down** in the garden, but he wasn't hurt.
If you feel dizzy, **lie down** for a few minutes.
sentences.translation: Boshingiz aylansa, bir necha daqiqa **yotib turing**.

sentences.text: **Look up** — there's a rainbow over the mountains!
Prices never **go down**, they only **go up**.
Could you **slow down**? You're driving too fast.
The sun **goes down** very early in December.
After the long walk we **sat down** on a bench by the river.
sentences.translation: Uzoq sayrdan keyin daryo bo'yidagi o'rindiqqa **o'tirdik**.

examples.title: **away** and **back**: go away, come back
examples.description: **away** — uzoqlashib, ketib («ketmoq», «qochib ketmoq»); **back** — qaytib («qaytib kelmoq», «qaytib bormoq»).

sentences.text: **Go away**, please — I'm trying to sleep!
Tom **went away** for the weekend, so his flat is empty.
sentences.translation: Tom dam olish kunlariga **jo'nab ketdi**, shuning uchun kvartirasi bo'sh.

sentences.text: What time will you **be back**?
Our dog **ran away** last week, but it **came back** two days later.
sentences.translation: Itimiz o'tgan hafta **qochib ketdi**, lekin ikki kundan keyin **qaytib keldi**.

sentences.text: I left my phone in the café, so I had to **go back**.
sentences.translation: Telefonimni kafeda qoldirib ketibman, shuning uchun **qaytib borishga** majbur bo'ldim.

sentences.text: Dilnoza **moved away** from Bukhara when she was ten.
Can you **call back** later? I'm in a meeting.
Many birds **fly away** when it gets cold.
Don't **walk away** when I'm talking to you!
Sarah **got back** from her holiday late last night.
sentences.translation: Sara ta'tildan kecha yarim tunda **qaytib keldi**.

examples.title: **on** and **off**: get on, get off, take off
examples.description: **get on** / **get off** — transportga chiqmoq / tushmoq; **take off** — samolyot ko'tarilmoq; **go on** — davom etmoq; **go off** — chiroq o'chmoq, budilnik jiringlamoq.

sentences.text: We **got on** the bus at Chorsu and **got off** near the university.
Our plane **took off** two hours late.
The little boy **fell off** his bike and cried.
sentences.translation: Kichkina bola velosipeddan **yiqilib tushdi** va yig'ladi.

sentences.text: Please **go on** — I'm listening.
Our meeting **went on** until nine o'clock.
**Hold on**! I need to find my keys.
The lights suddenly **went off** and the room was dark.
sentences.translation: To'satdan chiroqlar **o'chib qoldi**, xona qorong'i bo'lib qoldi.

sentences.text: The heating **comes on** automatically at six in the morning.
Be careful when you **get off** the train.
James's alarm **went off** at five, but he didn't wake up.
sentences.translation: Jeymsning budilnigi soat beshda **jiringladi**, lekin u uyg'onmadi.

examples.title: Everyday life: wake up, hurry up, grow up
examples.description: Kundalik hayotdagi frazali fe'llar. **wake up** (uyg'onmoq) va **get up** (o'rnidan turmoq) farqiga e'tibor bering; **stay up** — kech yotmoq, **set off** — yo'lga chiqmoq.

sentences.text: I **woke up** at six, but I didn't **get up** until seven.
**Hurry up**, or we'll miss the beginning of the film!
sentences.translation: **Tezroq bo'l**, bo'lmasa filmning boshini o'tkazib yuboramiz!

sentences.text: Children **grow up** so fast these days!
We **stayed up** until two o'clock watching the football.
**Calm down** — it's only a small problem.
**Cheer up**! Everything will be fine tomorrow.
Emma **works out** at the gym three times a week.
sentences.translation: Emma haftasiga uch marta sport zalida **shug'ullanadi**.

sentences.text: Aziz **grew up** in a small village near Samarkand.
Do you usually **get up** early at the weekend?
We **set off** early to avoid the traffic.

examples.title: Problems and warnings: break down, look out
examples.description: Muammo va ogohlantirish: **break down** (buzilib qolmoq), **look out** / **watch out** (ehtiyot bo'l!), **give up** (taslim bo'lmoq), **fall over** (yiqilmoq), **go off** (ovqat aynimoq), **speak up** (balandroq gapirmoq).

sentences.text: Our car **broke down** on the way to Bukhara.
**Look out**! There's a car coming!
**Watch out**, the floor in the kitchen is still wet.
The exercise was very difficult, but I didn't **give up**.
sentences.translation: Mashq juda qiyin edi, lekin men **bo'sh kelmadim**.

sentences.text: Bekzod slipped on the ice and **fell over**.
The washing machine has **broken down** again!
Don't **give up** — you're nearly there!
The milk **has gone off** — don't drink it!
**Speak up**, please — we can't hear you at the back.
If the car **breaks down** again, we'll buy a new one.

examples.title: Phrasal verb + preposition: come back **from** ...
examples.description: Frazali fe'ldan keyin predlog: come back **from**, run away **from**, look out **of**, get out **of**, look up **at**. Ba'zilari yaxlit ma'noli: get on **with** (chiqishmoq), look forward **to**, run out **of** (tugab qolmoq).

sentences.text: When did you **come back from** Manchester?
A thief **ran away from** the police.
Madina **looked out of** the window and saw the snow.
sentences.translation: Madina derazadan **tashqariga qaradi** va qorni ko'rdi.

sentences.text: **Get out of** the car, quickly!
We **went out for** dinner on Friday to celebrate.
sentences.translation: Juma kuni nishonlash uchun kechki ovqatga **tashqariga chiqdik**.

sentences.text: Do you **get on with** your new flatmates?
I'm **looking forward to** the holidays.
Tom **walked up to** the reception desk and asked for his key.
We've **run out of** milk, so I'm going to the shop.
sentences.translation: Sutimiz **tugab qolibdi**, shuning uchun do'konga ketyapman.

sentences.text: Sarah **looked up at** the sky and smiled.
sentences.translation: Sara **boshini ko'tarib** osmonga qaradi va jilmaydi.

examples.title: Dialogue: a bad morning
examples.description: Ishga kechikkan hamkasb bilan suhbat: **break down**, **get out**, **give up**, **sit down**, **go on**, **come back**, **calm down**.

sentences.text: — Sorry I'm late. My car **broke down** on the motorway.
— Oh no! Did you **get out** and look at the engine?
— Yes, but I know nothing about cars, so I **gave up** quickly.
sentences.translation: — Ha, lekin mashinalardan hech narsa tushunmayman, shuning uchun tezda **qo'l siltadim**.

sentences.text: — So how did you **get back** to town?
— A kind man **pulled over** and gave me a lift.
sentences.translation: — Bir mehribon odam yo'l chetiga **to'xtab**, meni olib keldi.

sentences.text: — Lucky you! **Sit down** and have some tea.
— Thanks. Has the meeting finished, or is it still **going on**?
sentences.translation: — Rahmat. Majlis tugadimi yoki hali **davom etyaptimi**?

sentences.text: — They're having a break. Everyone **went out** for coffee five minutes ago.
sentences.translation: — Tanaffus qilishyapti. Hamma besh daqiqa oldin qahva ichgani **chiqib ketdi**.

sentences.text: — Great. When they **come back**, I'll explain everything.
— Good idea. And **calm down** — nobody is angry with you.
sentences.translation: — Yaxshi fikr. **Tinchlaning** — hech kim sizdan xafa emas.
